learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the method and knowledge required to describe, understand and design industrial production and storage systems, and to define their maintenance criteria.
Learn how to efficiently use project management tools by means of provided statistic basics.

Learn the structure and operating principle of industrial plants in terms of: organization and management of the transformation of raw material into finished product, reliability of complex systems, role of human resources and industrial automation, production flows and layout, KPI and performance measurements.
Apply acquired knowledge in a real context of design, as well as in multidisciplinary or non-familiar areas, through practical classroom exercises.

Apply acquired knowledge to the industrialization of a production process, starting from the feasibility study, defining the best production structure and management, assessing the possibility of using automated operations to replace manual ones and controlling the process through KPIs.

Understand and critically evaluate the main production systems (forced and not-forced technological processes, production or assembly, manual or automated); analyze existing systems and assess their performances and adequacy, assess the impact of strategic, planning and operational decisions, and measure plant performances.
Acquire the specific vocabulary inherent to production plants.
Communicate the main contents of the course, both written and orally, such as ideas, engineering issues and related solutions.
Communicate knowledge through appropriate tools, solving numerical problems using common methods in the industry such as tables, diagrams, flow charts, and numerical spreadsheets.
Deepen knowledge of production plants through the autonomous consultation of specialized books, scientific or divulgative journals, even outside the topics explained during lectures.

syllabus_topics: General criteria for designing and realizing the main production plants
Classification of production plants, with and without a constrained technological cycle
Manual and automated manufacturing and assembly processes
Main performance indicators for monitoring the efficiency of industrial plants
Reliability theory for the maintenance of production systems
Impact of automation on these processes, both from a control and predictive maintenance perspective
Material handling and product storage systems
teaching_methods: Seminars by managers of multinational corporations

assessment_methods.method: Written test based on open questions

assessment_rules: Verification of knowledge takes place through a written test based on open questions, lasting 2.5 hours. The test usually consists of 11/12 questions that may relate to theoretical content, demonstrations, and exercises done during the course. The final grade is calculated by assigning a mark in the range 0-30 for each question and then performing the weighted average of the individual evaluations, with final ceiling to the next unit; the test is passed if it reaches a score of at least 18 points. '30 cum laude' is given to students who achieve the highest score on each item and use precise vocabulary.
